analysis.title: The Flow Show: DEM fatale
key_insights: Hartnett stays risk-off until central bank rate hikes end (41 in the past 6 months), the 10-year UST yield falls below 4.5% and oil falls below $80/bbl, which would reverse the tightening of financial conditions.
If Nov CPI and payrolls are weak, the Dec Fed/ECB/BoJ hikes could be the last hikes, and risk assets could start a year-end rally around Thanksgiving.
The report flags a 'double-top' in the S&P 500 Equal-Weighted Index (SPW) that nobody is calling a 'big top'.
NDX is down 15% over the past month and tech leaders broke: NVDA below $200, TSM below $400, MAGS below $70.
SPX holds above 7,000 and risk rotates (tech bonds, Europe, China, consumer) as long as recession odds stay low, with banks IXG holding $125, mid-caps MDY $666 and junk bonds JNK $92.

The report reads the Democratic midterm wins as a shift from populist capitalism to populist socialism, with taxes and regulation set to rise (negative for EPS), and calls the 2026 midterms the peak of AI equity concentration.
Midterm signals favor gold over oil, lower yields, tech bonds over tech stocks, consumer stocks over energy, small caps over monopolies, and long Europe and long China tech.

Gold is a buy ahead of the debt ceiling: Congress is sworn in Jan 3, the US hits the $41.1tn debt ceiling Feb 1 on the current 12-month run rate, and gold rose 12% and 17% in the 3 months before the 2011 and 2023 debt-ceiling standoffs.
Hyperscaler capex consensus is $239bn in '24, $412bn in '25, $820bn in '26 and $1.3tn in '27. FCF is $239bn, $191bn, -$63bn and -$252bn over the same years.
Hyperscaler financing has shifted: global debt issuance is $297bn YTD (vs $110bn in '25), equity issuance is $100bn YTD, and buybacks are $14bn YTD annualized (vs $90bn in '25).
Bond and credit markets want AI capex and issuance to slow. The report says slower capex favors MAGS 'spenders' over AI 'builders' such as semis and neoclouds.

Data centers are electorally unpopular (76% oppose, 24% favor in the SSRS poll), and many incoming Democratic governors ran on 'stop the data centers'. The report says the '28 AI capex forecast of about $2tn is a little too high.
Central banks have delivered 55 hikes this year versus 11 expected in January. The Fed hiked Sep 16 and the Dec 9 hike probability is 64%. Dec ECB is 76%, BOE 50% and BOJ 68%.

The report says oil needs to fall sharply for the tightening cycle to end before a credit event or recession. Its call is to sell energy, buy consumer, sell oil and buy bonds, and wait for lower oil prices and yields before adding risk 'bigtime'.

The 2027 scenarios are bubble, breadth and bust. Consensus conviction in the bubble case (50% of Oct FMS respondents predicting 'no landing') has peaked, but optimism on breadth is high (40% soft landing) and fear of a hard landing (6%) is too low.
Downward revisions are coming to '27 forecasts of 5% US nominal GDP and 45% global tech EPS growth (after 94% in '26).
Flows this week: $140.4bn to cash (7th biggest weekly inflow on record), $89.2bn to stocks, $11.6bn to bonds, $0.1bn to gold, $1.8bn out of crypto.
Global equities took in a record $265.6bn over 4 weeks ($317.1bn to passive). China stocks took in a record $85.9bn over 4 weeks, which the report attributes to 'national team' buying.
EM debt saw a $6.1bn outflow, its 6th biggest on record and the first since Jul'26.

The BofA Bull & Bear Indicator rose to 7.2 from 7.1 (Neutral signal), driven by large equity inflows. Global breadth is net 16% oversold and the buy signal needs net 88% oversold, which the report ties to SPX below 7323.
SOX is 17% below its 200-day moving average, and the report says 20-25% below has been a good entry point since '96.
BofA private clients hold 65.8% in stocks (3-month low), 17.7% in bonds (7-month high) and 9.3% in cash (record low).
The BofA FMS Cash Indicator reads 3.9% (Sell) and the EM Flow Trading Rule reads 4.3% (Sell).
2028 election odds on Polymarket: Democrats 68%, Republicans 31%. Ossoff leads the Democratic nomination at 28% and Vance leads the Republican at 35%.

Oil above $80/bbl and the 10-year UST yield above 4.5% keep financial conditions tight.
A bust in AI capex as bonds and voters end the boom, with credit tightening.
Negative hyperscaler free cash flow of -$63bn in '26 and -$252bn in '27 funded by record debt and equity issuance.
Regulation and tax increases under the new Democratic Congress and governors, including limits on data centers.
Downward revisions to '27 forecasts of 5% US nominal GDP and 45% global tech EPS growth.

A credit event or recession before the tightening cycle ends.

Chart 8 shows consensus hyperscaler capex of $412bn in '25, $820bn in '26 and $1.3tn in '27, and FCF of $191bn in '25, -$63bn in '26 and -$252bn in '27.

vol_and_positioning: The BofA Bull & Bear Indicator is at 7.2 (Neutral). Equity flow is at the 95th percentile (very bullish), FMS positioning is at 100% (very bullish) and global stock index breadth is at 21% (bearish).
Hedge fund positioning is at the 61st percentile, bond flow at 55% and credit market technicals at 53%.
The Global Breadth Rule is net 16% oversold in one place and -20.5% in the proprietary table. The buy signal needs net 88% oversold.
SOX is 17% below its 200-day moving average. Past entry points came at 20-25% below.
The Global Flow Trading Rule reads 0.9% (Neutral), the EM Flow Trading Rule reads 4.3% (Sell) and the FMS Cash Indicator reads 3.9% (Sell).
The report cites more bearish positioning in crude oil, the US dollar and gold futures, and weaker credit market technicals.
Cash inflow of $140.4bn was the 7th biggest weekly inflow on record. Treasuries saw their 19th straight week of inflows.
geopolitical: The Democratic midterm results are read as a shift toward taxes and regulation and less ability for Trump to direct resources, corporations and foreign governments toward winning the AI race with China.
The 2028 US presidential election is 733 days away. Polymarket has Democrats at 68% and Republicans at 31%.
The Spain election on Nov 29 is expected to flip from center-left to center-right.
Voters cite the war in Iran, cost of living and AI data centers as major factors in their vote.
China's 'national team' buying drove a record $85.9bn inflow to China stock funds over 4 weeks.
The report says high oil did not cause China to fold.
cross_bank_references: Per BofA Global FMS in July, 7/10 investors said no Fed hike before midterms.
Per SemiAnalysis, about 100 GW of new US data center capacity is expected online in the next 2 years.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus expects hyperscaler capex of $1.3tn in '27 and 15% SPX EPS growth. Goldilocks would unlock value in small and mid-caps and SPX ex-AI.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscaler FCF turns to -$252bn in '27 and is funded by record debt issuance. Bond markets want slower capex, and data centers are electorally unpopular.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Bond yields reset lower with no recession would bring AI stocks back, per the report. SPX below 7,000, or banks IXG below $125, mid-caps MDY below $666 and JNK below $92, would signal rising recession odds.

tension_points.theme: Fed and central bank hiking cycle
tension_points.bull_case: If inflation drops and the tightening cycle ends before a credit event, '27 stays Goldilocks with bullish breadth.
tension_points.bear_case: The Fed, ECB, BOE and BOJ are expected to hike in December, with oil above $80 and the 10-year above 4.5% tightening financial conditions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weak Nov CPI and payrolls would make the Dec hikes the last hikes. The risk-off stance holds until the 10-year UST yield is below 4.5% and oil is below $80/bbl.
